constraints: The repository can run security tests, regression tests, and static analysis.
The team can request a calibrated review of nuanced code quality.
Tool order is not part of the task contract.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the only valid output were one deterministic file with a fixed checksum, a behavioral rubric would add little value.
details.errorCorrection: A fixed tool order rejects valid solutions, prose does not prove repository state, and shared production trials contaminate evidence.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends clean isolated trials, outcome-based grading, deterministic checks where possible, and calibrated judgment for nuanced dimensions.
details.scenarioApplication: Run the repair in an isolated checkout, execute security and regression checks, and send the diff and rubric to a calibrated reviewer.
details.transfer: Grade required outcomes and safety boundaries, then add independent judgment only for dimensions deterministic checks cannot observe.

messages.text: A valid repair can use a different sequence, so sequence identity would be a brittle proxy.
An explanation can claim a fix without changing the vulnerable artifact.
Shared state contaminates trials and risks changing production during evaluation.
Deterministic checks verify the concrete security and regression contract.
A calibrated independent review can assess nuanced quality without turning one path into the requirement.

feedback.reason: Artifact checks prove the known security contract, while calibrated review covers nuanced behavior without requiring one brittle implementation path.

options.text: Grade the changed repository with deterministic security and regression checks, including static analysis.
Require the agent to use one recorded tool order even when the resulting artifact is equivalent.
Score the final explanation only and infer that the repository changed correctly.
Run all trials in the shared production checkout so the patch is realistic.
Use a calibrated rubric or fresh review for interaction and code-quality dimensions that automated checks cannot decide.

prompt: A code-review agent repairs a vulnerable authentication handler in an isolated repository, and valid implementations may use different tool sequences. Select TWO grading controls.

constraints: The task and grader disagree about the required path.
A reference implementation can test the harness contract.
Valid agent outputs were observed at another path.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the reference solution passed and the task contract were explicit, a 0% result would justify investigating model behavior or tool access.
details.errorCorrection: A larger model or manual impressions cannot repair a contradictory contract, and removing the path requirement makes the evaluation unfaithful.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic warns that ambiguous specifications create evaluation noise and recommends a reference solution to verify task and grader configuration.
details.scenarioApplication: Correct the declared path or grader expectation, run the reference migration, and only then compare model results.
details.transfer: Validate the evaluator’s own contract with a known-good result before interpreting a model score.

messages.text: Model size cannot resolve an unstated or contradictory file-path contract.
Removing a real output requirement hides the harness defect instead of fixing it.
Anecdotal impressions cannot establish whether the automated task and grader agree.

feedback.reason: The score is uninterpretable until task and grader agree and a known working solution passes the harness.

options.text: Switch to a larger model so it may infer the grader’s hidden path.
Remove the path assertion so the current score improves.
Align task and grader; make the reference solution pass, then rerun.
Average the 0% result with manual impressions from the engineers who ran the trials.

prompt: A coding-agent evaluation reports 0% pass across 100 migration trials because the task omits the required file path while the grader expects one exact path. A known working solution can be placed at the grader’s path. What should happen first?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A separate holdout can be periodically refreshed or access-controlled so repeated tuning does not turn it into another development set.
details.errorCorrection: Avoid both extremes: do not discard useful regression fixtures, and do not treat them as independent generalization evidence.
details.mechanismOrProperty: An evaluation set’s interpretation depends on its relationship to prompt examples and tuning data; fixture reuse is not universally invalid, but it limits what a score establishes.
details.scenarioApplication: Label the 24-case score as development/regression evidence and construct a disjoint holdout with representative claims, layouts, and source provenance.
details.transfer: Match each dataset’s use and independence boundary to the claim made from its score.

messages.text: Known fixtures can still detect regressions on their intended examples; they simply cannot stand in for independent generalization evidence.
Synthetic origin does not make cases independent once the exact examples are included in the prompt.
Paraphrased descendants can carry the same answers and patterns, so they do not automatically create an independent evaluation set.

feedback.reason: These fixtures still serve a valid known-case regression purpose, but their direct reuse in the prompt contaminates a claim about unseen-case performance. Maintain the regression suite and evaluate a separate, provenance-checked holdout.

options.text: Keep reused fixtures for regression; use unseen, independently sourced cases to support generalization claims.
Delete the regression suite because any fixture that appears in a prompt is unusable for future testing.
Keep reporting the 100% as holdout accuracy because the prompts are synthetic rather than production text.
Generate paraphrases from the same 24 cases and call them a holdout without checking whether they preserve the same cues.

prompt: A team uses 24 public synthetic cases both as few-shot prompt examples and as a continuous regression suite. Those cases catch formatting breaks after a prompt edit, but product leaders now cite the 100% score as evidence of performance on unseen claims. What is the correct interpretation and next evaluation step?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: After calibration, use automated or single-reviewer grading for clearer cases and retain double review where judgments remain consequential or ambiguous.
details.errorCorrection: Seniority, averaging, or a larger aggregate does not establish that reviewers share the intended boundary.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Human review is a measurement process; agreement should be assessed on the dimensions that matter, not only as a global percentage.
details.scenarioApplication: Create examples for mixed source support and partial completion, double-score those cases blind, record why disagreements resolve one way, and report agreement by category.
details.transfer: Locate disagreement clusters, refine the rubric at that boundary, and verify calibration before expanding grader use.

messages.text: Discarding the disagreements hides a systematic rubric boundary and prevents the team from knowing whether the lead is applying it consistently.
An average can conceal a categorical disagreement about evidence or partial completion rather than resolve its meaning.
More cases do not correct an ambiguous category boundary; they may simply dilute the problematic slice in the aggregate.

feedback.reason: Agreement is high overall but fails on a consequential, identifiable slice. Improve the rubric and adjudication record for that slice before using the score as a stable grader.

options.text: Use the lead reviewer’s labels as ground truth and discard the independent ratings.
Average the numeric scores from both reviewers and treat the mean as an adjudicated label.
Adjudicate disagreement, report uncertain outcomes, and test a revised rubric on held-out mixed cases.
Add more cases until the overall 92% agreement rises, leaving the rubric unchanged.

prompt: Two trained reviewers independently grade 80 long-form assistant answers with the same rubric. They agree on 92% overall, but disagree on 31% of answers involving mixed evidence and partial completion; a lead reviewer currently resolves every disagreement without recording a reason. What should the evaluation team improve first?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Automated entailment checks are themselves imperfect, so report their validated scope and retain sampling on difficult claims.
details.errorCorrection: A citation string can be well-formed yet irrelevant; swapping all checks for one broad judge may hide both kinds of defects.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Evaluation needs a grader for each assertion; syntactic validity and factual support are different outcomes.
details.scenarioApplication: Bind claim spans to retrieved passages where feasible, evaluate the support relation, and send ambiguous cases to a calibrated reviewer while retaining JSON/schema tests.
details.transfer: List what each grader actually observes, then add coverage for high-impact assertions it misses.

messages.text: Removing known deterministic checks loses useful coverage, and one opaque score may reproduce the same citation blind spot.
Citation length does not establish that the cited span supports the claim.
Document membership alone does not prove that the cited passage entails the answer.

feedback.reason: The grader currently tests citation presence and output shape, not evidence support. Keep the deterministic format checks and add a distinct support assertion with calibrated review where entailment is not mechanically decidable.

options.text: Audit whether cited passages support each claim; citation presence alone does not establish correctness.
Replace the structural grader with a single LLM judge that returns pass or fail for the whole answer.
Require longer citations so at least one sentence is likely to contain the right evidence.
Treat a non-empty source ID as sufficient because the model has already selected a retrieved document.

prompt: A customer-support evaluation’s deterministic grader checks valid JSON, required field names, and whether every response has a non-empty citation string. A release scores 100%, but reviewers find citations that point to unrelated passages. Which harness change best addresses the blind spot?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The added sample does not imply equal deployment volumes; weights should follow a documented production population and be revisited when it shifts.
details.errorCorrection: Neither a simple presence check nor a weighted average resolves the small-slice evidence gap.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A dataset should reflect its intended population while still exposing subgroups whose errors carry distinct risk.
details.scenarioApplication: Collect additional Japanese examples across relevant tasks, preserve English and Spanish coverage, publish per-language estimates with uncertainty, and separately show a production-weighted overall result.
details.transfer: Report both representative overall performance and the slices whose failures the aggregate could conceal.

messages.text: Presence alone does not make the sample representative, and five Japanese cases cannot establish its error rate reliably.
A weighted aggregate can reflect traffic mix but can still hide the severe Japanese failure and its uncertainty.
Equal counts may help estimate slices but do not represent production weighting, and removing common cases discards relevant behavior.

feedback.reason: The current sample is dominated beyond the production mix and under-samples the language with the observed severe error. Expand and label the strata, report slice uncertainty, and keep an aggregate from masking a consequential slice.

options.text: Keep the current overall score because the evaluation contains all three languages.
Sample to the production language mix and separately evaluate the underrepresented high-risk language.
Weight Japanese to 10% and report only the weighted average so the slice has the same influence as in production.
Add many Japanese cases and remove English cases until all language counts are equal, then report only the unweighted mean.

prompt: A production assistant is used 70% in English, 20% in Spanish, and 10% in Japanese. The current 100-case evaluation is 95% English and reports a 94% overall score; Japanese has only five cases and one severe unsupported answer. What should the next dataset and report do?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a group is too small to estimate reliably, add cases or report uncertainty instead of silently dropping it.
details.errorCorrection: Do not equate refusal with failure or omit refusals and partial outputs from the report.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A task and grader must define how abstention and partial evidence contribute to outcomes; the denominator should match the eligible request population.
details.scenarioApplication: Label evidence sufficiency, grade supported answers on the answerable group, appropriate refusals on the unanswerable group, and qualification on partial-evidence cases; show all three results and the overall decision rule.
details.transfer: Make every valid completion mode observable in the grader and denominator.

messages.text: This excludes two required behaviors and can hide unsupported answers or inappropriate refusals.
That incorrectly penalizes appropriate refusals when evidence is absent and does not distinguish partial support.
Removing those cases abandons explicit product requirements and biases the evaluation toward fully answerable requests.

feedback.reason: The policy defines valid behavior for answerable, unanswerable and partially supported requests. Excluding two groups makes the 98% result incomplete; score each declared outcome and publish the category breakdown.

options.text: Accuracy on the 120 answered requests only, since refusals and partial answers do not contain a factual claim.
Report answerable, unanswerable and partial cases separately against their appropriate outcomes.
One overall pass rate that counts all refusals and partial answers as failures.
Remove the unanswerable and partial-evidence cases so the remaining task is easier to grade.

prompt: A document assistant is tested on 200 requests: 120 have sufficient evidence, 40 are deliberately unanswerable, and 40 have only partial evidence. The report shows 98% accuracy after excluding refusals and partial responses from its denominator. Product policy requires supported answers, appropriate refusals, and explicit qualification when evidence is incomplete. What should the harness measure?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the release owner revises the policy threshold, evaluate that as an explicit new criterion with its own decision record.
details.errorCorrection: Do not substitute a large relative lift for the stated minimum or lower the threshold after observing results.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Evaluation reports should retain both absolute criteria and comparative deltas; a gain over a weak baseline does not prove an acceptable outcome.
details.scenarioApplication: Report the +13-point change and the 91% absolute score separately, then check each required slice against the no-more-than-2-point regression rule.
details.transfer: Use comparative deltas to understand improvement and absolute gates to decide whether the result is fit for use.

messages.text: A relative improvement does not satisfy the 93% absolute pass condition.
The contract includes a slice-regression bound, which must be checked and cannot be waived by the aggregate gain.
Changing the release criterion after seeing the result would redefine success rather than evaluate against the existing contract.

feedback.reason: The candidate improves substantially over baseline but remains below the absolute 93% gate. Relative change and release readiness answer different questions.

options.text: Release the new model because its 13-point improvement is large.
Release only to the overall cohort because every individual slice is less important than the gain.
Require the absolute gate; report relative gain separately as a secondary comparison.
Lower the threshold to the prior model’s 79% so the comparison reflects the baseline.

prompt: A new model raises the evaluation score from 78% to 91% on a 300-case suite. The release contract requires at least 93% absolute pass and no more than a 2-point regression on any required slice. The prior model scores 79% on the same suite. What does the evaluation support?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Keep structural assertions deterministic where possible and use the calibrated grader only for dimensions that need judgment.
details.errorCorrection: Do not assume unchanged topic means unchanged grading validity, and do not replace evidence checks with fluency/style penalties.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Model-based graders are flexible but need calibration for the actual task and outcome dimensions they score.
details.scenarioApplication: Build blinded labels for complete answers, partial evidence, appropriate refusal and citation support; compare grader decisions and inspect disagreements before using it in a release decision.
details.transfer: Revalidate a grader when the task shape or outcome population changes.

messages.text: The task and outcome distribution changed, and the observed blind spot shows the old calibration does not cover the new behavior.
Style or confidence language is not a reliable substitute for evidence support, partial completion or appropriate refusal.
That omits newly required outcomes and would make the release comparison incomplete.

feedback.reason: The grader’s calibration set covered a narrower answer shape, and the spot check identifies a blind spot in newly added outcomes. Validate it on representative expert-labeled cases before relying on the scores.

options.text: Keep the grader because the model and answer domain are unchanged.
Calibrate the grader on refusal, partial-answer and citation outcomes before comparing systems.
Add a stricter confidence-word penalty so the grader rejects any answer that sounds uncertain.
Use the grader only on the easiest complete answers and exclude all partial/refusal cases from the comparison.

prompt: An LLM grader was calibrated on short, complete support answers. The product now accepts multi-turn cases with partial evidence, refusals, and citations; a spot check finds that the grader rewards fluent unsupported guesses in this new set. What should happen before using its scores for the next release comparison?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A group-disjoint set may have fewer examples and wider uncertainty; collect additional suppliers rather than silently returning to a row split.
details.errorCorrection: More rows from the same groups or a different invoice number do not create an independent new-supplier test.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Evaluation independence follows the unit that can share answer cues or layout structure; row-level randomization can leak across correlated documents.
details.scenarioApplication: Partition by supplier and template family, inspect monthly revision lineage for near-duplicates, and report the current split as within-known-group performance.
details.transfer: Choose split boundaries that isolate the source of generalization the score is meant to support.

messages.text: The holdout still shares supplier and layout groups with tuning, so more rows mainly increase precision for the wrong population.
Changing invoice numbers does not prevent shared supplier templates and revision cues from crossing the split.
Removing training groups after seeing the existing score changes the evaluation and still requires a fresh, group-aware run.

feedback.reason: The row-level split tests new invoices from known supplier and template families, not generalization to new suppliers. Preserve it for that narrower purpose and build a group-disjoint evaluation for the claim leaders want to make.

options.text: Keep the random split and increase the number of rows, since each invoice is a separate example.
Keep random-split regression; add a supplier-disjoint holdout for new-supplier generalization.
Move only the newest invoice from each supplier to holdout; shared template families do not affect generalization if invoice numbers differ.
Remove all repeated suppliers from training and report the current holdout score without rerunning it.

prompt: A claims extractor is tuned on 600 invoice rows from 12 suppliers. The random 20% holdout contains different invoices, but every supplier and document-template family appears in both tuning and holdout; several suppliers reuse near-identical layouts across monthly revisions. The team wants to claim performance on new suppliers. What should the next evaluation do?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Adjudicate representative cases, test the revised rubric on held-out examples, then rerun both candidates under the same definitions.
details.errorCorrection: Neither all refusals nor all answers are automatically correct.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Evaluation criteria should reflect supported task outcomes and label definitions.
details.scenarioApplication: Tuning against the scored refusal cases risks adapting to the test set rather than validating general behavior.
details.transfer: Keep evaluator version and denominator consistent for comparisons.

messages.text: A separate table still leaves the primary comparison unable to distinguish unsafe abstention from a missed supported handoff.
This treats two different workflow outcomes alike and leaves the handoff contract outside the candidate comparison.
Reusing evaluation examples for tuning and comparison leaks the test into development even if the held-back subset is smaller.

feedback.reason: The evaluator collapsed distinct outcomes into one label. A calibrated rubric must distinguish safe refusal, correct handoff, and avoidable failure before it can compare systems.

options.text: Keep the old answer-rate measure as the primary headline, but add a separate refusal and handoff table so the new rubric does not interrupt the trend.
Define and adjudicate answerable, unsafe, and handoff outcomes; test the rubric on a held-out set before comparing candidates.
Score a refusal as correct when the request is unsafe, and score a handoff as neutral until the receiving team reports an outcome.
Use the newly observed refusal cases for prompt tuning, then reserve a smaller random subset of the same cases to compare the revised score.

prompt: An evaluator update turns every refusal into a failure. Reviewers find that some cases are genuinely unsafe to answer, while others require a supported handoff; the candidate’s answer rate rises but the new score falls. What is the best next evaluation step?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Preserve separate correctness and safety outcomes so one does not mask the other.
details.errorCorrection: Disabling the block would increase risk and is unnecessary for scoring the attempt.
details.mechanismOrProperty: An outcome-only grader misses unsafe intermediate behavior when a policy control blocks the attempted action.
details.scenarioApplication: The test should record whether disallowed tools were attempted, not only whether side effects completed.
details.transfer: Evaluate the complete tool-using trajectory when the task includes side-effect boundaries.

messages.text: A separate count does not prevent a prohibited attempt from receiving a passing safety grade.
The attempted deletion crossed the prohibited boundary even though the environment prevented its effect.
Removing the control allows a real destructive action; evaluation should detect the attempted call while preserving the safeguard.

feedback.reason: The final text hides a prohibited action attempt. The evaluation must score the action trace as well as answer correctness.

options.text: Keep the run passed because the control blocked the deletion; add a separate counter showing how often the agent proposes a prohibited mutation.
Keep final-answer grading and add a tool-use penalty only when a prohibited call returns data or changes state.
Add trace-based safety criteria that fail prohibited mutation attempts, even when the environment blocks them and the final answer is correct.
Use a reversible sandbox without the blocking stub, then restore the test data after the run to observe the agent’s actual behavior.

prompt: A billing-agent test ends with the correct read-only report. The tool trace shows it first attempted `delete_customer`; a policy stub blocked the call. The evaluator grades only the final text and marks the run passed. What should change?

constraints: Fixture origin can be traced and near-duplicates removed.
A reference solution can verify the task and grader before a split is frozen.
The holdout must represent unseen layouts.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: With no tuning and complete production representation, a separate holdout would add less evidence, though a reference check would remain useful.
details.errorCorrection: Duplicating tuned templates and postponing unseen cases inflate evidence without testing generalization; wording similarity is not the extraction contract.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends a known working reference solution to verify task and grader configuration; provenance, deduplication, and holdout separation are scenario controls.
details.scenarioApplication: Freeze a deduplicated holdout after checking its source and layout distribution, run the reference, and publish holdout results separately from tuning results.
details.transfer: Protect evaluation evidence from tuning leakage and validate the frozen split before using it to compare systems.

messages.text: Copies increase volume but preserve the same tuning leakage.
A tuning score cannot estimate unseen-layout behavior.
Surface wording is not a reliable proxy for extracted fields or claim state.

feedback.reason: Tuned examples cannot be the sole evidence for generalization; an independent, traceable holdout tests unseen layouts and a valid task/grader contract.

options.text: Add more copies of tuned templates so the 100% score has a larger sample.
Use a provenance-tracked, deduplicated holdout and validate a reference before scoring it.
Use the tuning score as the release baseline and add unseen layouts only after deployment.
Replace deterministic field checks with a judge that rewards similar wording to the tuned examples.

prompt: A claims extractor scores 100% after prompt tuning, but tuning and scored fixtures share templates and the suite has no provenance or frozen holdout. Production contains unseen document layouts. Which evaluation change is best?

constraints: Trial-level tool responses, transcripts, and outcomes are retained.
The harness can identify whether external state differed.
The team needs stability evidence rather than a best-run headline.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If runs and tools were deterministic and the reference passed, one clean trial per case could be sufficient for this harness.
details.errorCorrection: A best run, untraceable average, or removal of the external dependency discards the production behavior being evaluated.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic defines evaluations through tasks, trials, graders, transcripts, outcomes, and a harness, supporting explicit evidence across each trial.
details.scenarioApplication: Repeat each case under recorded lookup conditions, retain transcripts, classify failures, and report a distribution rather than the most favorable aggregate.
details.transfer: When outcomes vary, preserve trial-level evidence and report variance and causes instead of compressing them into a lucky score.

messages.text: A favorable run confuses a sample with stable capability and omits the observed variance.
Averages without state evidence cannot explain which failures were external or model-driven.
Removing a production dependency changes the evaluated contract rather than diagnosing it.

feedback.reason: The run variance is itself evidence; repeated isolated trials and retained state reveal whether failures come from stochastic behavior or external conditions.

options.text: Publish the 9/10 run as the baseline and rerun only after users report failures.
Average the best and worst runs without retaining the tool responses.
Repeat isolated trials and report distributions with retained transcripts and tool state.
Disable the external lookup and report the deterministic score as production capability while documenting the changed environment.

prompt: A tool-using agent passes 9 of 10 trials on one run, then ranges from 5 to 9 on repeated runs because an external lookup is variable. What should the harness report?

constraints: Option order can be randomized in the harness.
Human labels and judge rationales can be retained for calibration.
Objective assertions can use deterministic checks.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If every assertion had a deterministic checker and no model judgment were used, presentation order would not affect evaluation.
details.errorCorrection: Reproducibility of a biased order, shortening answers, or preserving the favored position does not test the intended code behavior.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends deterministic graders where possible and human review for validation and calibration; order and verbosity probes are scenario controls.
details.scenarioApplication: Randomize option order, compare judge labels with calibrated human labels, retain rationales, and route material disagreement for review.
details.transfer: Validate an evaluator for bias against the target outcome before trusting its aggregate scores.

messages.text: A repeatable position or verbosity bias remains a validity problem.
Editing answers to fit a biased judge changes the candidates instead of fixing the evaluator.
Consistently favoring one position makes the order confound permanent.

feedback.reason: A stable score can still be systematically biased by position and verbosity, so the judge needs controlled presentation and calibration against the intended outcome.

options.text: Keep the judge because its average score remains stable across repeated runs and the current presentation order is consistent for every candidate.
Shorten every candidate answer until the verbosity effect disappears.
Put the preferred answer first consistently so the judge’s ranking is reproducible.
Randomize order, calibrate judge labels against human review, and use deterministic checks for objective claims.

prompt: A model judge rates the same code explanations higher when they are longer and when the preferred answer is listed first; calibrated human reviewers disagree. What should the team change first?

constraints: The transcript records the denied destructive call and its real target.
The final report and allowed read path pass their outcome checks.
The contract treats an unauthorized attempt as a safety failure.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the first call were an allowed read_customer operation producing the same report, the varied sequence could pass within the authorized action set.
details.errorCorrection: A denial is not evidence of respectful tool choice, intent is not observable proof, and requiring one read sequence confuses safety with path identity.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic lists tool-call verification among code-based graders, supports binary or hybrid scoring, and cautions that rigidly requiring one valid path is brittle; the prohibition is scenario policy.
details.scenarioApplication: Mark the safety gate failed, preserve the transcript and report-test result, and allow authorized read-only variations among otherwise compliant trials.
details.transfer: When a task prohibits an action, grade attempted actions as a separate gate even if a downstream control blocks the effect.

messages.text: A downstream denial prevents state change but does not make the attempted delete compliant.
Intent cannot override the recorded action and explicit prohibition.
The contract prohibits the action itself; exact path matching is unnecessary for authorized reads.

feedback.reason: The attempted destructive action violates an explicit safety gate even though downstream policy prevented state change; report correctness can remain a separate dimension.

options.text: Fail for the unauthorized destructive attempt; record separate credit for the correct report.
Pass because the policy server blocked the delete and the report is exact.
Pass if a reviewer believes the agent intended to test authorization.
Require the exact read-query sequence and ignore the denied call because sequence is the only objective evidence.

prompt: A coding agent must produce a correct read-only billing report. It first calls delete_customer with a real ID; the policy server denies the call. It then uses an allowed read query and returns the exact report, and all report tests pass. The contract prohibits attempting destructive actions. What result is correct?

constraints: The tool-safety cases, ordinary cases, tool-call traces, and independent evaluator are available; the destructive behavior is governed by a separate guardrail.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the evaluation already contained a provenance-tracked, balanced high-impact slice with independent traces and passing safety gates, the ordinary aggregate could be combined with it for release.
details.errorCorrection: Production monitoring would discover a high-blast-radius failure after release, and aggregate accuracy hides the missing trigger/refusal behavior. The competing action therefore leaves the stated decision boundary unresolved.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends testing cases where a behavior should occur and where it should not to avoid one-sided optimization. The case-specific population, thresholds, roles, and authority limits are supplied by this scenario rather than by the provider documentation.
details.scenarioApplication: Expand or hold out a risk-stratified set with both allowed and refused destructive-action cases, grade tool traces deterministically, and block the release until the safety slice passes its own gate.
details.transfer: Give rare consequential behaviors their own balanced tests and release boundary instead of letting volume hide them.

messages.text: Production monitoring would discover a high-blast-radius failure only after release.
More ordinary cases cannot compensate for missing positive and negative coverage of the dangerous behavior.
A holistic score does not supply deterministic evidence that the tool was allowed or refused under the right condition.
Required control: Add a risk-stratified safety slice with balanced cases where the destructive action is allowed and where it must be refused.
Required control: Grade tool traces deterministically and block release until the high-impact safety slice passes its own gate.

feedback.reason: Expand or hold out a risk-stratified set with both allowed and refused destructive-action cases, grade tool traces deterministically, and block the release until the safety slice passes its own gate. The decisive constraint is A rare high-impact behavior needs balanced positive and negative cases before the aggregate can support release; ordinary-case volume cannot compensate for missing safety coverage.

options.text: Ship because the 99% aggregate and ordinary-case tool traces pass, then monitor destructive attempts in production.
Add more ordinary cases to make the aggregate larger before deciding whether the two destructive cases matter.
Add a risk-stratified safety slice with balanced cases where the destructive action is allowed and where it must be refused.
Use a single holistic model judge over the existing cases and treat its confidence as the missing refusal evidence.
Grade tool traces deterministically and block release until the high-impact safety slice passes its own gate.

prompt: An agent passes 99% of a 500-case evaluation, but only two cases exercise a high-impact destructive tool attempt and neither covers a negative case where the tool must be refused. The release owner asks whether the aggregate pass is sufficient. Select TWO: Which controls are needed before this aggregate can support release?

constraints: Independent billing fixtures, final report fields, authorization traces, tool arguments, and the old gold trace are available; the revised path performs no write or destructive operation.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the task explicitly required one exact tool sequence for audit or side-effect ordering, the trace difference would be a contract failure and the trial would need remediation.
details.errorCorrection: A historical path is not a business or safety requirement by itself; failing it would reward incidental implementation order and discourage safe authorized alternatives. The competing action therefore leaves the stated decision boundary unresolved.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends clean isolated trials, outcome-based grading, deterministic checks where possible, and calibrated model graders for nuanced dimensions. The case-specific population, thresholds, roles, and authority limits are supplied by this scenario rather than by the provider documentation.
details.scenarioApplication: Pass the revised trial for the correct report and authorized read-only behavior, record the path variation, and update the gold trace or grader only if the sequence was never a contract; keep the destructive attempt as a separate failure evidence case.
details.transfer: Grade the declared outcome and safety boundary, while treating implementation traces as evidence only when the contract requires them.

messages.text: An incidental historical order is not a business or safety requirement when the authorized outcome is equivalent.
A destructive call violates the safety contract even when the final report is correct.
A correct report cannot prove that the agent stayed within the required authorization boundary.
Required control: Grade the final billing report and the authorization and no-side-effect contract rather than requiring one incidental read-only path.
Required control: Update the gold trace or grader only if the historical sequence was never a contract, and keep the destructive attempt as separate failure evidence.

feedback.reason: Pass the revised trial for the correct report and authorized read-only behavior, record the path variation, and update the gold trace or grader only if the sequence was never a contract; keep the destructive attempt as a separate failure evidence case. The decisive constraint is The safety and business contract requires a correct report without unauthorized side effects, not one incidental read-only call sequence; a changed authorized path should pass outcome and constraint grading unless the exact sequence is itself a declared requirement.

options.text: Grade the final billing report and the authorization and no-side-effect contract rather than requiring one incidental read-only path.
Fail the revised trial because its tool trace differs from the historical gold sequence even though the report and authorization checks pass.
Accept any tool sequence that produces the report, including a delete call, because the final text is the only required artifact.
Update the gold trace or grader only if the historical sequence was never a contract, and keep the destructive attempt as separate failure evidence.
Grade the report alone and omit tool permissions from the result because the revised path is read-only.

prompt: A coding agent must produce a correct read-only billing report. In the original evaluation, one trial attempted delete_customer with a real ID before producing the report; a revised implementation now reaches the same report through a different fully authorized read-only lookup path, while the evaluator still expects the original tool sequence. Select TWO: Which grading decisions best handle the revised trial?

constraints: Field extraction and claim state have objective checks.
Explanation quality needs a domain rubric and human calibration.
The small set is available now and can be expanded from reviewed cases.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If every task had a deterministic structured answer and a large clean corpus, exact checks could carry most of the harness.
